source.title: Wieszcz-XIX: A 3.1-Billion-Word Corpus of Pre-1918 Polish and Temporally Bounded Language Models Trained From Scratch

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures held-out cross-entropy across a parameter-size ladder, a loss measure and scaling intervention comparable to the original scaling-law work, but on small historical-Polish models and a narrow size range.
record.gate_note: The study reports a three-model parameter ladder and compares additional training on repeated data with increasing model size. It does not test extrapolation to a much larger run or a compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. The architecture is held fixed across the ladder, so it does not test architecture sensitivity. Results cited from other papers are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study's own held-out cross-entropy falls across a three-rung parameter ladder (47.1M–349.1M) trained on identical data, steps and seed. It also reports that the fitted exponent changes with the evaluation protocol. The setting is new: from-scratch historical Polish trained for two epochs, so the models are data-constrained. Scaling is a side result of a corpus paper, and three points under one order of magnitude cannot test the power-law form itself, so T3 fits better than T1.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors report per-rung gains of 0.196 and 0.232 nats, about twice the gain of a second pass over the data. They frame this as quantifying Muennighoff et al.'s data-constrained regime for this corpus. They note the three-point floor-law fit has no residual and that α changes with the evaluation protocol, so they report rung differences rather than the exponent. They do not explicitly say the ladder is 'not evidence for a general scaling law'; that phrasing is the reader's.
record.recipe_differences: Uses held-out cross-entropy over a decoder-only model-size ladder, but applies it to three small from-scratch Polish models trained on a historical corpus, with fixed tokens, steps and seed. The authors fit a floor power law through only three points and report sensitivity to evaluation protocol.
record.method_sensitivity: The fitted exponent changes with evaluation method: 0.202 for the dense held-out protocol versus 0.355 for the twenty-window in-training probe. The held-out source changes absolute loss levels, although the reported rung-to-rung gains are nearly unchanged.

fits_no_version.finding: Moving up one rung gains 0.196 and 0.232 nats, about twice the 0.093–0.119 nats from a second epoch plus decay. The stable-phase second-epoch gain alone is about a quarter of the rung gain. The second-epoch gain grows with model size (0.047, 0.054, 0.063).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In a data-constrained regime, adding parameters reduces held-out loss more than repeating the data for a second epoch.

fits_no_version.finding: Train–held-out gap at the end of the two-epoch run grows with size: +0.025, +0.027, +0.067 nats (Fig. 2 caption).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under repeated data, the generalisation gap grows with model size.

record.problems: The parameter ladder has only three points over 47.1M–349.1M parameters; a three-parameter fit through three points has no residual. Each rung was trained once from a single seed, so run-to-run variation is unknown. All rungs were trained for exactly two epochs, and the authors describe the setting as data-constrained. The exponent differs between the dense evaluation and in-training probe.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible scaling results left out. The reported loss values for additional checkpoints are represented by the epoch-gain results in r10–r12; other corpus, temporal-bound, generation and bias findings do not measure scaling-law versions.

untested.parts: Power-law form (three points, exactly fitted). Range of several orders of magnitude (tested span is about 0.87 decades). Token and compute scaling. Run-to-run variance (single seed per rung).
No small-run fit is used to predict a larger run.
No fixed-compute sweep over parameter/token split. The matched-cost 107M-one-epoch vs 47M-two-epoch comparison is a single anecdote.
Depth and width co-vary with size; there is no shape variation at fixed N.
Text only. The regime is repeated data (two epochs), but no power-law form is fitted within it.
No downstream tasks. Generation quality is judged qualitatively by one author.
Parameter counting, schedule, data and fitting-method alternatives. Compute-optimal split. Curvature away from a power law.

missing.what: Tokenizer-independent held-out loss per rung in bits per byte: 1.333, 1.249, 1.149. Useful for comparing across vocabularies.
Matched-cost comparison: 107M after one epoch (3.009, ~16.9h) beats 47M after two epochs (3.1009, 18.4h).
missing.versions: none (bears loosely on V3 but is not a fixed-compute sweep)

record.verdict_notes: Tranche changed from T1 to T3: same measure as the originals, but a new setting, and the ladder is too short to test the law's form. The record's V1 limits_scope label was removed, because narrow range and no residual are untested parts rather than shown failures. Nothing in the results shows the version failing. r10–r17 were unlinked or set to cannot_determine. Per-log-N gain shrinks slightly (≈0.24 vs ≈0.20 nats per e-fold), consistent with a floor law, but three points cannot distinguish forms. Each rung was trained once from seed 1337, so the reported intervals are measurement error only.

versions.untested_parts: Tests parameter scaling over 47.1M–349.1M parameters with training tokens held fixed; does not test several orders of magnitude, compute scaling, or token scaling without repeated-data and schedule confounds.
No prediction fitted on small runs is evaluated against a much larger held-out run.
No fixed-compute search for the loss-minimising parameter/token split.
Architecture details are not varied at fixed parameter count.
Text pretraining only; the study compares a second data pass but does not test whether the same power-law form holds across repeated-data regimes, modalities, fine-tuning or transfer.
No downstream task performance is measured against scale or pretraining loss.

Shows a different fitted parameter exponent under the dense held-out evaluation and the in-training probe; does not test compute-optimal allocation, parameter-counting alternatives, or broader data and schedule choices.

rows.subject: xix-47M to xix-349M ladder
rows.operation_detail: Fit a power law with irreducible floor through the three dense-protocol parameter-size results
rows.note: The authors state that three parameters through three points leave no residual.
rows.check: A three-parameter fit L=E+AN^−α through exactly three points has no residual, so α=0.202 cannot confirm or refute the power-law form for V1. For V7 it serves as the reference value for r14, not as an effect on its own.

rows.subject: xix-47M to xix-349M ladder
rows.operation_detail: Fit the same checkpoints using the in-training probe rather than the dense held-out protocol
rows.note: The paper explicitly reports that the exponent changes with the evaluation protocol.
rows.check: α moves from 0.202 (dense) to 0.355 (twenty-window probe, 20,480 tokens) on the same checkpoints. Both fits are exactly determined, so the shift also reflects the small probe's noise. Baseline is correctly the dense fit.

relationships.condition: Three rungs 47.1M→107M→349M, same 6.69B-token split, two epochs, single seed, pooled and per-source dense held-out evaluation
relationships.reason: Pooled held-out CE falls 3.1009→2.9046→2.6726 (r1–r3). Internet Archive (r4–r6) and Wolne Lektury (r7–r9) fall by nearly identical per-rung amounts. Only monotone decrease over less than one decade is shown, not the power-law form.
relationships.display_finding: Pooled held-out cross-entropy falls from 3.1009 through 2.9046 to 2.6726, with similar per-scale decreases across both sources, establishing monotonic decline over less than one decade.
